digest.component_or_area: Jira Data Center adapter / transport layer
propositions: The DC transport must implement TicketTransport plus SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, and SupportsAbsenceProbe roles, built atop pycontribs/jira behind an opt-in [jira-datacenter] extra and imported lazily so rebar's dependency-free contract holds.
Every transport method returns raw payload shapes (dicts with {key, fields, ...}) that rebar's existing mappers consume, unwrapping the pycontribs JIRA object model at the adapter boundary.
Auth uses Personal Access Token (DC 8.14+) read env-only from JIRA_PAT as bearer token; url and project come from typed config; malformed config raises ConfigError rather than degrading to env-only.

HTTP errors are never retried (exactly 1 attempt); transient connectivity faults (requests.ConnectionError, socket.timeout, builtin TimeoutError) are retried with 2s/5s backoff mirroring acli_rest._rest_urlopen_with_retry; assignee failures raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError.

TLS validation rejects non-https base_url with ConfigError unless allow_insecure=true; certificate verification is never disabled (verify is never False); ca_bundle config supports internal CAs; allow_insecure affects URL scheme check only, not cert verification.

resolved_statuses config sets the absence-probe's resolved-status classifier, defaulting to {Resolved, Done, Cancelled} when unset, because self-hosted DC workflows can name resolved states arbitrarily and hardcoded Cloud/DIG names would misclassify resolved issues as PRESENT_FILTERED.
